subject: Day 1: Where wisdom starts
title: Wisdom begins with taking God seriously.
body:
Proverbs opens by telling us why it exists: to make us wise. And then it hands us the key in verse 7. The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge. That does not mean being scared of God. It means taking Him seriously, the way you take gravity seriously.

Everything else this month builds on that one idea. Wise people start with God.
q_young: What is something you know a lot about? Who taught you?
What do you think it means to take God seriously?
q_teen: What is the difference between being smart and being wise?
Verse 7 says fools despise wisdom. Why do you think people ignore good advice even when they know it is good?
family_challenge: Everyone shares one thing they want to get wiser about this month.
tip: No table needed. The car works great: read the verses at pickup or on the way to practice and talk on the drive.

subject: Day 2: Digging for treasure
title: Wisdom goes to the people who search for it.
body:
Chapter 2 says to look for wisdom like silver, to search for it like hidden treasure. Treasure does not fall on you. You dig.

God is not hiding wisdom from us. He promises to give it to anyone who honestly looks. But looking is the part we skip.
q_young: If you could dig up any treasure, what would you want to find?
Where do you think a person digs to find wisdom?
q_teen: What is something valuable that took you real effort to get? Was it worth it?
What would searching for wisdom actually look like in your week?
family_challenge: Hide something small in the house or car and let the kids hunt for it. Then talk about verse 4: search for wisdom like that.
tip: Let a kid read the verses out loud. Kids remember what they read to the family far better than what they are read.

subject: Day 3: Trust with your whole heart
title: Trust God with all your heart, not just the easy parts.
body:
Proverbs 3:5-6 might be the most famous verses in the book. Trust in the LORD with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding.

Everyone trusts something: their plan, their feelings, their own smarts. Proverbs says trust the One who sees the whole road, and He will keep your paths straight.
q_young: Who do you trust to catch you if you fell? Why them?
What is something you trust God to take care of?
q_teen: What is one area where you would rather trust your own plan than ask God? Be honest.
What makes trusting God hard when you cannot see how something ends?
family_challenge: Have everyone memorize Proverbs 3:5 together tonight. Race to say it fastest.
tip: Play the chapter on the Bible app while everyone eats or rides. Audio counts.

subject: Day 4: Guard your heart
title: What you let into your heart runs your whole life.
body:
Chapter 4 gives one of the biggest commands in the book: above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it.

We lock the front door but leave our hearts wide open to whatever wants in. What you watch, hear, and dwell on becomes what you do.
q_young: What kinds of things do we lock up or protect? Why?
What is something good you want to keep in your heart?
q_teen: What actually gets into your heart most each day, and does it make you better or worse?
If everything you do flows from your heart, what does your week say is in there?
family_challenge: As a family, name one thing you will let in more of this month, and one thing you will guard against.
tip: Breakfast works as well as dinner. Attach it to a meal you already share.

subject: Day 5: Keeping promises
title: Faithful people keep their promises even when it costs them.
body:
Chapter 5 is about faithfulness, staying true to the people you have committed to. It is written to grown-ups about marriage, but the root is for everyone: promises matter.

God sees everything we do, verse 21 says. Faithfulness is who you are when no one is checking.
q_young: What is a promise someone kept to you? How did it feel?
Why is it hard to keep a promise sometimes?
q_teen: Have you ever had someone break a promise to you? What did it change?
What is one commitment you want to be known for keeping?
family_challenge: Each person makes one small, real promise to the family for this week. Write them down. Check back Friday.
tip: With little ones, one or two verses is plenty. You do not need the whole chapter to have the conversation.

subject: Day 6: Watch the ant
title: Nobody has to make the ant work. Be like the ant.
body:
Proverbs 6 says: go watch the ants. Nobody supervises them. Nobody nags them. They just see the work and do it.

Laziness never announces itself. It whispers a little more sleep, a little more scrolling. Proverbs says the wise see what needs doing and start.
q_young: What do ants do all day? What would happen if they all stopped?
What is one job you can do without being asked?
q_teen: What is the thing you put off the most, and what does it cost you?
What is the difference between resting and being lazy?
family_challenge: Tonight everyone does one chore nobody asked them to do. Compare notes tomorrow.
tip: Let the kids ask the questions tonight. Hand a young reader the questions and let them run it.

subject: Day 7: Avoiding traps
title: Wisdom sees the trap before you step in it.
body:
Chapter 7 tells a story of someone walking straight into a trap because it looked good at first. The whole chapter is a warning: temptation never looks like a trap at the start.

Wisdom is looking down the road. Not just is this fun now, but where does this path end?
q_young: How does a mouse trap work? Why does the mouse go to it?
What is something that looks fun but can hurt you?
q_teen: What is a real trap for people your age that looks harmless at first?
How do you actually get out of a tempting situation? What is your move?
family_challenge: Make a family code word anyone can text or say when they feel stuck in a bad situation and need a way out, no questions asked.
tip: Older kid not home? Text them the teen question and let them answer by text. It still counts.

subject: Day 8: Wisdom is shouting
title: God's wisdom is not hidden. It is calling out to anyone who will listen.
body:
In chapter 8, wisdom stands at the crossroads and shouts. She is not whispering in a secret club. She is in the street, calling everyone.

Most of the time we do not lack wisdom. We lack the listening. The voice is there: parents, Scripture, wise friends, that nudge in your gut you keep overriding.
q_young: If wisdom had a voice, what do you think it would sound like?
Who in your life gives you really good advice?
q_teen: When was the last time you knew the right thing and did the opposite? What drowned out the voice?
Verse 11 says wisdom is worth more than rubies. Do you actually believe that? What do people our age treat as more valuable?
family_challenge: Everyone names one person they will actually ask for advice this month, and what they will ask.
tip: Missed a day or three? No guilt. Just do today's. The goal is talking about wisdom as a family, not a perfect streak.

subject: Day 9: Two invitations
title: Every day, wisdom and foolishness both invite you to dinner.
body:
Chapter 9 pictures two houses. Wisdom builds hers and sets a table. Folly sits at her door and calls out too. Same street, two invitations, every single day.

You cannot accept both. Every choice is an RSVP.
q_young: If two friends invited you over at the same time, how would you pick?
What is one wise choice you made this week?
q_teen: What does Folly's invitation look like for you specifically? It is different for everyone.
Verse 8 says wise people love correction. How do you react when someone corrects you?
family_challenge: At dinner or in the car, list three choices tomorrow will bring and decide the wise RSVP for each, out loud, in advance.
tip: No table needed. The car works great: read the verses at pickup or on the way to practice and talk on the drive.

subject: Day 10: Words that build, words that break
title: Your mouth is either a fountain of life or a wrecking ball.
body:
Chapter 10 begins the one-liners, and a bunch of them are about the mouth. The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, verse 11 says. And verse 19: when words are many, sin is not absent.

Every family has a word culture. Today is a good day to look at ours.
q_young: What is the nicest thing someone said to you this week?
How do you feel when someone uses mean words at you?
q_teen: Is your default with your siblings building or tearing? What would they say?
Verse 19 says fewer words means fewer sins. When should you have just stayed quiet recently?
family_challenge: Fountain night: everyone says one true, kind sentence about each person present. No repeats, no jokes.
tip: Let a kid read the verses out loud. Kids remember what they read to the family far better than what they are read.

subject: Day 11: Honest scales
title: God loves honesty in the small stuff nobody sees.
body:
Chapter 11 opens with dishonest scales, a merchant quietly cheating customers a little at a time. The LORD detests it. He delights in accuracy.

Most dishonesty is small. The half-answer to a parent. Rounding up your effort. God cares about the small honest thing because that is where character is built.
q_young: Why is it wrong to cheat in a game, even a little?
Have you ever told the truth when it was hard? What happened?
q_teen: What is a small dishonesty people your age think does not count?
Verse 3 says integrity guides you. How does being known as honest actually make life easier?
family_challenge: Truth check: each person shares one small thing they were not fully honest about lately. No punishments tonight, just clean slates.
tip: Play the chapter on the Bible app while everyone eats or rides. Audio counts.

subject: Day 12: Who you listen to
title: Wise people love being corrected. Fools hate it.
body:
Verse 1 of chapter 12 is blunt: whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but whoever hates correction is stupid. Proverbs does not soften it.

Correction is a gift wrapped in something uncomfortable. The wise open it anyway.
q_young: When mom or dad corrects you, what is it for?
Can you remember a rule that kept you safe?
q_teen: What is your honest first reaction to correction: listen, argue, or shut down?
Who is allowed to correct you? If the answer is nobody, what does that say?
family_challenge: Parents go first tonight: share a correction you received as an adult and how it helped you. Then invite the kids to share one.
tip: Breakfast works as well as dinner. Attach it to a meal you already share.

subject: Day 13: Choose your walking partners
title: Walk with the wise and you get wiser. Walk with fools and you get hurt.
body:
Proverbs 13:20 is one to memorize as a family: walk with the wise and become wise, for a companion of fools suffers harm.

You become like the people you spend time with. Not instantly. Gradually, like walking a trail together.
q_young: Who are your best friends? What do you like doing together?
How do friends change how we act?
q_teen: Think about your closest three friends. Are they making you wiser or pulling you down?
What kind of walking partner are YOU for your friends?
family_challenge: Everyone names one wise person they want more time with, and the family figures out how to make one of those happen this month.
tip: With little ones, one or two verses is plenty. You do not need the whole chapter to have the conversation.

subject: Day 14: Building your house
title: Every day you are either building your home or tearing it down.
body:
Chapter 14 starts with a picture: the wise woman builds her house, but the foolish one tears hers down with her own hands. That is true of everyone in a family, not just moms.

Every kindness is a brick laid. Every eye-roll, slammed door, and cutting remark pulls one out. Houses go up slowly and come down fast.
q_young: What do you need to build a strong house?
What is one thing that makes our family strong?
q_teen: What do you personally add to this family when you are at your best?
What is one habit of yours that tears at the house? You do not have to say it out loud, but name it to yourself.
family_challenge: Build something together tonight or this weekend: blocks with littles, a puzzle, pancakes. While you build, talk about what builds a family.
tip: Let the kids ask the questions tonight. Hand a young reader the questions and let them run it.

subject: Day 15: The gentle answer
title: A gentle answer turns away anger. A harsh word stirs it up.
body:
Proverbs 15:1 might be the most practical verse in the whole book for a household. A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.

Every argument has a moment where it could go either way. One person going gentle, on purpose, changes the whole room.
q_young: Show me your gentle voice. Now show me your grumpy voice. Which one makes people listen?
What can you do when someone is angry at you?
q_teen: Think of your last blow-up with someone in this house. Where was the moment it could have gone differently?
Why does going gentle feel like losing? Is it?
family_challenge: Practice round: act out someone taking your seat, and respond two ways, harsh then gentle. Laugh about it. Then use the gentle one for real this week.
tip: Older kid not home? Text them the teen question and let them answer by text. It still counts.

subject: Day 16: Who directs your steps
title: You can make your plans, but God directs your steps.
body:
Proverbs 16:9 says we make our plans, but the LORD establishes our steps. Plans are good. Proverbs is not against planning. It is against planning like you are God.

Hold your plans with an open hand. Some of the best things in your life will be interruptions.
q_young: What do you want to be when you grow up?
Has a day ever turned out different than you thought, but better?
q_teen: What is your current plan for your life? How would you handle God redirecting it?
Verse 18 warns pride comes before a fall. Where does pride sneak into your plans?
family_challenge: Everyone shares one plan they have, then prays one sentence: God, direct my steps.
tip: Missed a day or three? No guilt. Just do today's. The goal is talking about wisdom as a family, not a perfect streak.

subject: Day 17: A friend at all times
title: Real friends love you on your worst day, and a cheerful heart is good medicine.
body:
Two gems today. Verse 17: a friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity. Verse 22: a cheerful heart is good medicine.

Family is who shows up on the hard days. And laughter in a house is not extra, it is medicine.
q_young: Who came to help you last time you were sad or hurt?
What makes our whole family laugh?
q_teen: Are you an all-times friend, or a good-times friend?
Who in your life needs a brother or sister born for adversity right now?
family_challenge: Medicine night: watch or tell the funniest family story you have. Someone will say I remember when, and let it roll from there.
tip: No table needed. The car works great: read the verses at pickup or on the way to practice and talk on the drive.

subject: Day 18: Listen before you answer
title: Answering before you listen is folly and shame.
body:
Proverbs 18:13: to answer before listening, that is folly and shame. We all do it. We are loading our reply while the other person is still talking.

Listening is love with its mouth closed. It is also how the wise learn anything.
q_young: How can you tell when someone is really listening to you?
What are good listening ears like?
q_teen: Who actually listens all the way to the end of your sentences? How does it feel?
In your last argument, could you repeat back what the other person actually said?
family_challenge: The echo game at dinner or in the car: before you can answer anyone, repeat their point back in your own words first. Try it for ten minutes.
tip: Let a kid read the verses out loud. Kids remember what they read to the family far better than what they are read.

subject: Day 19: Patience and the long way
title: A patient person has great understanding. Hot tempers make everything worse.
body:
Chapter 19 keeps circling patience. Verse 11: a person's wisdom yields patience; it is to one's glory to overlook an offense.

Overlooking an offense does not mean pretending. It means you are strong enough not to need every fight.
q_young: What is the hardest thing to wait for?
What happens when someone loses their temper over something little?
q_teen: What is the last offense you could have overlooked but did not? Was the fight worth it?
Where does impatience cost you most: family, friends, school?
family_challenge: Pick the family flashpoint (getting out the door, bedtime, chores) and agree on one patient move everyone will try there this week.
tip: Play the chapter on the Bible app while everyone eats or rides. Audio counts.

subject: Day 20: Known by your actions
title: Even a child is known by their actions.
body:
Proverbs 20:11 says even small children are known by whether their conduct is pure and right. What you do is your reputation, at any age.

Everyone in the family already has a track record: with teachers, coaches, friends, each other. The good news is a track record is built one action at a time, starting today.
q_young: What do you want your teacher to say about you?
What is one good thing you did today?
q_teen: What are you currently known for? Is it what you want to be known for?
One action this week could start changing your reputation where it needs it. What is it?
family_challenge: Each person picks one word they want to be known for this year. Write them on a card and stick it on the fridge or the dashboard.
tip: Breakfast works as well as dinner. Attach it to a meal you already share.

subject: Day 21: Doing right beats looking right
title: God cares more about doing what is right than looking religious.
body:
Proverbs 21:3: to do what is right and just is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice. In other words, God is not impressed by the show.

He would rather have honest homework than a loud prayer, and a kept promise than a perfect church outfit.
q_young: What is the difference between doing a chore and just saying you did?
What is something right you can do for someone tomorrow?
q_teen: Where is it tempting to look good instead of be good, at church, online, at school?
What would change if God graded your week by verse 3?
family_challenge: Secret mission: everyone does one right and just thing for somebody outside the family this week without telling them. Report back Sunday.
tip: With little ones, one or two verses is plenty. You do not need the whole chapter to have the conversation.

subject: Day 22: A good name and open hands
title: A good name is worth more than riches, and generous people are blessed.
body:
Two anchors in chapter 22. Verse 1: a good name is more desirable than great riches. And verse 9: the generous will themselves be blessed, for they share their food with the poor.

Your name and your hands. Guard the first, open the second.
q_young: If you could give one of your toys to a kid with none, which one would you give?
What makes someone a giver?
q_teen: Would you trade your reputation for money? People do it in small ways all the time. Where?
What do you have plenty of that someone else lacks: stuff, time, skill?
family_challenge: Family generosity project: pick something real this week. A bag of groceries for the food pantry, outgrown clothes, or a GiveSendGo campaign the kids help choose.
tip: Let the kids ask the questions tonight. Hand a young reader the questions and let them run it.

subject: Day 23: Apply your heart
title: Put your whole heart into learning, and do not envy people doing wrong.
body:
Proverbs 23:12 says apply your heart to instruction and your ears to words of knowledge. Not just your seat in the chair, your heart.

And verse 17 warns: do not let your heart envy sinners. Shortcuts look shiny. They always cost more than they promise.
q_young: What is your favorite thing to learn about?
What does it mean to try with your whole heart?
q_teen: Where are you coasting right now, present but not really trying?
Who do you secretly envy, and what is the real cost of what they are doing?
family_challenge: Everyone names the one class, skill, or subject getting half their heart, and one way to give it a full heart this week.
tip: Older kid not home? Text them the teen question and let them answer by text. It still counts.

subject: Day 24: By wisdom a house is built
title: Wisdom builds a home and fills its rooms with good things.
body:
Proverbs 24:3-4: by wisdom a house is built, and through understanding it is established; through knowledge its rooms are filled with rare and beautiful treasures.

The treasures that fill a home are not from the store. They are memories, safety, laughter, faith. That is what you have been building around this table and in this car all month.
q_young: What is your favorite room in our house and why?
What treasure does our family have that money cannot buy?
q_teen: Verse 16 says the righteous fall seven times and rise again. What have you gotten back up from?
What rare and beautiful thing do you want your future home to be full of?
family_challenge: Draw or describe your dream family room, then have each person name the invisible treasures they would fill it with.
tip: Missed a day or three? No guilt. Just do today's. The goal is talking about wisdom as a family, not a perfect streak.

subject: Day 25: Self-control is your wall
title: A person without self-control is a city with broken-down walls.
body:
In Bible times, a city without walls was defenseless. Anything could walk in. Proverbs 25:28 says that is a person without self-control.

Self-control is not about being no fun. Walls are what make the fun inside safe.
q_young: Why did old cities have big walls?
What is something hard to stop doing once you start?
q_teen: Where is your wall broken right now: temper, phone, food, words?
What is one brick you could lay this week, one specific limit you set for yourself?
family_challenge: Everyone picks one self-control brick for the week and says it out loud. Check on each other kindly, no policing.
tip: No table needed. The car works great: read the verses at pickup or on the way to practice and talk on the drive.

subject: Day 26: Do not feed the fire
title: Without gossip, a quarrel dies down like a fire without wood.
body:
Proverbs 26:20: without wood a fire goes out; without gossip a quarrel dies down. Every conflict is a fire, and gossip is the firewood.

Families and friend groups stay at war because somebody keeps carrying wood. Be the one who puts the logs down.
q_young: What does a campfire need to keep burning?
What happens when we tattle just to get someone in trouble?
q_teen: Be honest: when friends start talking about someone, what do you usually do?
What quarrel in your world would die out if people just stopped feeding it?
family_challenge: Family rule proposal: we do not talk badly about people who are not in the room. Discuss it, adjust it, adopt it.
tip: Let a kid read the verses out loud. Kids remember what they read to the family far better than what they are read.

subject: Day 27: Iron sharpens iron
title: As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another.
body:
Proverbs 27:17 is the friendship verse: as iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another. Sharpening involves friction. Sparks, even.

The people who make you better are not always the ones who make you comfortable. And verse 6 adds: wounds from a friend can be trusted.
q_young: How do you make a pencil sharp? What happens to a dull one?
Who helps you get better at something?
q_teen: Who sharpens you, tells you the truth even when it stings?
Who are you sharpening? Or do you only hang out where there is no friction at all?
family_challenge: Sharpening circle: each person tells the person on their right one strength they see in them, and one gentle push to grow.
tip: Play the chapter on the Bible app while everyone eats or rides. Audio counts.

subject: Day 28: Bold as a lion
title: The righteous are as bold as a lion, and confession brings mercy.
body:
Two lions in chapter 28. Verse 1: the righteous are as bold as a lion. Doing right gives you a spine.

And verse 13: whoever conceals their sins does not prosper, but the one who confesses and renounces them finds mercy. Hiding it eats you. Confessing it frees you.
q_young: What animal do you think is the bravest? Why?
Why does it feel better after you say sorry?
q_teen: What would you do this month if you were bold as a lion?
Is there anything you are carrying hidden? Verse 13 says mercy is on the other side of saying it.
family_challenge: Courage round: everyone names one brave right thing they will do this week. Parents included. Follow up next week.
tip: Breakfast works as well as dinner. Attach it to a meal you already share.

subject: Day 29: A fool gives full vent
title: Fools give full vent to their rage, but the wise bring calm.
body:
Proverbs 29:11: fools give full vent to their rage, but the wise bring calm in the end. Venting feels honest. Proverbs calls it foolish.

Bringing calm is not stuffing your feelings. It is being the thermostat instead of the thermometer, setting the temperature instead of just reporting it.
q_young: What does your body feel like when you get really mad?
What helps you calm down?
q_teen: Are you a thermostat or a thermometer in this family?
What is your actual plan for the next time rage shows up? Name the steps.
family_challenge: Build the family calm-down plan together: three steps anyone can use mid-meltdown. Post it where the meltdowns happen.
tip: With little ones, one or two verses is plenty. You do not need the whole chapter to have the conversation.

subject: Day 30: Two honest prayers
title: Give me neither poverty nor riches. Keep me honest and dependent on You.
body:
Proverbs 30 is a humble chapter. Agur admits what he does not know, then prays two things: keep lies far from me, and give me neither poverty nor riches, just my daily bread.

That prayer trusts God for enough. Not everything. Enough.
q_young: What are three things our family has that we can thank God for?
What is the difference between what you want and what you need?
q_teen: Would you honestly pray do not make me rich? Why is that hard?
What does enough look like for you?
family_challenge: Gratitude alphabet in the car or at the table: go A to Z naming things God gave your family. See how far you get.
tip: Let the kids ask the questions tonight. Hand a young reader the questions and let them run it.

subject: Day 31: A home built on wisdom
title: A person and a family that fear the LORD are worth more than anything.
body:
The last chapter paints a person of strength and dignity whose family stands up and calls her blessed. The closing line of the whole book brings us back to day one: charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting, but a person who fears the LORD is to be praised.

Thirty-one days. You read the entire book of wisdom together, around tables and in cars and wherever life happened. That is not a small thing. That is training hearts. Keep going, one conversation at a time.
q_young: What was your favorite day of this challenge?
What is one wise thing you learned this month?
q_teen: Which chapter actually changed something you did this month?
If your family kept one habit from these 31 days, which should it be?
family_challenge: Celebrate. Special dessert or a drive for ice cream. Each person shares the one thing from Proverbs they want to carry for life. Then grab your certificate.
tip: Older kid not home? Text them the teen question and let them answer by text. It still counts.
